title: Language Transformers and Meaning · Level 3
slo: Explain how a language transformer represents relationships among words.

exercises.question_text: Which results are associated with attention? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Attention assigns token representations using context. Each token can therefore reflect its relation to others.

options.text: More closely aligned vectors for similar contexts
options.rationale: Tokens used in similar contexts receive more closely aligned embeddings. This captures semantic relationships.
Attention uses relationships among tokens in context. Those relationships influence the assigned representations.

options.text: Pixel labels for every image region
options.rationale: Pixel labels are outputs of image segmentation. Attention in this context models language-token relationships.
options.better_fit: This is appropriate for a semantic-segmentation system.

feedback.intrinsic: The result would shift from language meaning to image labeling.
feedback.instructional: Attention models contextual relationships among tokens.

exercises.question_text: What produces transformer encoder vectors with many dimensions?

options.rationale: Transformer encoders create high-dimensional vectors through complex linear-algebra calculations. The dimensions encode contextual relationships.
Bounding boxes locate objects in images. They do not create transformer encoder embeddings.
options.better_fit: Use bounding-box calculations for object detection.

feedback.intrinsic: Vector creation would be confused with object localization.
feedback.instructional: Encoder vectors arise from linear-algebra calculations.

options.rationale: Patch extraction prepares image portions for a vision transformer. It is not the calculation that creates encoder-vector dimensions.
options.better_fit: Use patch extraction when converting an image into ViT inputs.

feedback.intrinsic: An input-preparation step would replace vector computation.
feedback.instructional: High-dimensional encoder vectors come from linear algebra.

options.rationale: Tokenization identifies language units. It does not perform the complex calculations that create high-dimensional encoder vectors.
options.better_fit: Use tokenization to prepare text for language-model processing.

feedback.intrinsic: The embedding calculation would be omitted.
feedback.instructional: Tokens become encoder vectors through linear-algebra calculations.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Encoder embeddings are produced through complex linear algebra.

exercises.question_text: A vector is a single language word represented by a model.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: This mixes a token with its representation.

exercises.explanation: Correct. A word is a token, while a vector is numeric.

exercises.question_text: Transformer encoder vectors have many dimensions that encode complex contextual relationships.

feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Transformer encoder vectors are high-dimensional and contextual.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Many dimensions encode complex contextual relationships.

exercises.question_text: Which statements describe a vision transformer? Select all that apply.

options.text: It is trained on many images.
options.rationale: A vision transformer is trained on image data. It applies the transformer approach to images.
A ViT extracts image patches from an image. Each patch contains a portion of pixel values.

options.text: It converts patches into linear vectors.
options.rationale: A vision transformer converts image patches into linear vectors. These vectors are then processed using the transformer approach.

options.text: It uses text tokens instead of image patches.
options.rationale: Text tokens are language-model inputs. A ViT begins with image patches from visual data.
options.better_fit: This fits a language transformer processing written text.

feedback.instructional: Vision transformers use patches, not text tokens.

exercises.explanation: Correct. ViTs process images as patches converted into vectors.

exercises.question_text: What does attention use to assign a token representation?

options.text: Its relationships to other tokens in context
options.rationale: Attention considers how a token relates to other tokens in context. Those relationships shape its representation.
Pixel values belong to image data. Language attention uses relationships among tokens.
options.better_fit: Pixel values are relevant when processing image patches.

feedback.instructional: Attention uses token relationships, not pixels.

options.rationale: Position can contribute information, but attention is defined here by relationships among tokens. Position alone cannot capture contextual meaning.
options.better_fit: Position information can help a model distinguish ordering in a sequence.

feedback.intrinsic: The representation would omit surrounding-word relationships.
feedback.instructional: Attention depends on context between tokens.

options.rationale: Translation is an NLP task that a model may support. It is not the mechanism attention uses to assign representations.
options.better_fit: Translation is a downstream language task for a semantic language model.

feedback.intrinsic: A task outcome would replace the contextual mechanism.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Attention relies on contextual token relationships.

exercises.question_text: A word, phrase, or other language unit represented by a model is a ___.

parts.text: A word, phrase, or other language unit represented by a model is a

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The response names a representation rather than the unit.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Use token for a word, phrase, or other language unit.

exercises.explanation: A token is the language unit that a model represents.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The model's purpose is not expressed clearly.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Connect the model to embedding relationships and token similarities.

exercises.correct_answer: A semantic language model uses embedding relationships to represent language-token similarities.
exercises.explanation: Embedding relationships represent similarities among language tokens.

exercises.question_text: Which characteristics describe a language transformer? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Language transformers use embeddings. These vectors represent attributes of language tokens.
Attention models relationships among tokens in context. This helps a transformer represent language meaning.

options.text: It processes large volumes of data.
options.rationale: A transformer architecture can process large volumes of data. Its attention and embedding mechanisms help model relationships in that data.

options.text: It extracts image patches as its language input.
options.rationale: Image patches are portions of image pixels used by vision transformers. A language transformer works with language tokens.
options.better_fit: This is appropriate for a vision transformer processing photographs.

feedback.intrinsic: Language would be treated as image regions.
feedback.instructional: Language transformers use tokens, embeddings, and attention.

exercises.explanation: Correct. These are key transformer characteristics.

exercises.question_text: A model that represents similarities between language tokens through embedding relationships is a ___.

parts.text: A model that represents similarities between language tokens through embedding relationships is a

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The response names a different model or mechanism.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Use semantic language model for language-token similarity representation.

exercises.explanation: A semantic language model represents token similarities through embedding relationships.

exercises.question_text: Arrange the words into a complete statement.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The statement does not clearly express the architecture's function.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Start with the transformer, then name its methods and goal.

exercises.correct_answer: A transformer uses embeddings and attention to model language context.
exercises.explanation: A transformer uses embeddings and attention to model language context.

options.text: A portion of an image containing pixel values
options.rationale: An image patch is a portion of image pixel values. A vision transformer converts each patch to a vector.
A word or phrase unit is a language token. An image patch is visual input made from pixels.
options.better_fit: This describes a token used in language processing.

feedback.intrinsic: A photo would be treated as language.
feedback.instructional: Patches contain pixels; tokens are language units.

options.text: A semantic vector for a token
options.rationale: A semantic vector is an embedding. A patch may be converted into a vector, but the patch is the original image portion.
options.better_fit: This describes an embedding for a token or visual patch.

feedback.intrinsic: The visual input would be confused with its representation.
feedback.instructional: A patch is pixel data before conversion to a vector.

options.rationale: A token relationship weight belongs to attention. An image patch is a portion of visual pixel data.
options.better_fit: This is relevant when attention relates tokens in context.

feedback.intrinsic: The image input would be mistaken for a context mechanism.
feedback.instructional: Image patches are portions of an image.

exercises.explanation: Correct. An image patch is a portion of pixel values.
